admission.justification: The policy is carried across the model that validates and the channel that stores it, so one place cannot tighten the pair alone. It guards a plausible and costly error: a validator that rejects a whole composer report because its new fields are unusable would blank the tray's measured placement for that page, and one that accepts half a pair would place the tray at a width the box does not have. Three channel cases hold it, including eight rejected shapes.

applicability: Composer reports an in-frame plug-in posts to the dashboard's tray channel, on every frame page - the Chats view and the document/review column - provided the report's vertical fields are the ones the parser admits.
conditions: The pair is admitted only when both left and width are finite numbers and width is greater than 0.

A report whose vertical fields are finite and admissible, meaning a finite top, height and frameHeight with height >= 0 and frameHeight > 0, and which carries no pair, is valid and yields the vertical-only measured edge; the pair rules never waive those vertical guards.
A report whose vertical fields fail those guards is rejected whatever its pair says.

The pair-less shape also occurs with the current plug-in: pick.ts rounds left and width, so a box narrower than half a pixel posts width 0 and the validator drops it. An older plug-in that has not been provisioned posts the vertical edge alone.
exclusions: The dock's placement once an extent is accepted, which INV-S3NMAZ owns.
The ar.tray-space reservation height and the scroll root it pads.
Pick messages and their provenance, and every other tray message type.
Event origin and window trust, which the frame controller supplies before parsing.

evidence: dashboard/src/cockpit/frameTrayChannel.test.ts::"takes the box's own left and width as a pair"; dashboard/src/cockpit/frameTrayChannel.test.ts::"drops a partial, non-finite or non-positive pair and keeps the vertical edge" (eight vectors); dashboard/src/cockpit/frameTrayChannel.test.ts::"keeps a composer message without the pair valid"; those cases drive PaseoFrameControl.receive -> parsePluginMessage -> receiveFrameTray, i.e. validator and channel on one path; npx vitest run src/tray/TrayDock.test.tsx src/cockpit/frameTrayChannel.test.ts src/cockpit/paseoPluginPick.test.ts -> 35 passed / 35

statement: The dashboard accepts the box's left and width only as a pair of finite numbers whose width is greater than 0, keeps a composer message that carries no pair valid, and drops a partial, non-finite or non-positive pair while the vertical edge survives.
